stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +102.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $43.03 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 136 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 136 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-13.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-30) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.excerpt: A number of tech figures want the board of the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
stories.lead:
Allies of Jensen Huang are trying to rally support for the former Nvidia boss to get his job back after resigning last week over a scandal involving extramarital affairs, one involving an alleged Chinese spy.

SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, are among those backing a campaign to get the AI chip giant's board to "Bring Jensen Back".

Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after the emergence of two affairs, one of whom was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.

stories.title: As millions lose food aid nationwide, this SNAP office is doubling up as a food pantry
stories.excerpt: The cuts and changes to SNAP have been difficult for government workers who take pride in helping others. In San Diego, workers said they couldn't sit back while their neighbors went hungry.
stories.lead:
SAN DIEGO, CALIF. — It should have been her day off. Instead, early Saturday morning, Rosa Rodarte was back at the social service office where she works, pushing carts of food and loading them into people's cars.

Rodarte's official job is to help people apply for programs like food assistance. But lately, she's been simply helping people get food.

"We have the same goal," she says. "We want to make sure everybody is being helped and not judged."

stories.title: Five EU countries expected to announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
stories.excerpt: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to announce a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
stories.lead:
Five EU countries are expected to announce the creation of a migrant deportation centre in the landlocked African country Rwanda, according to diplomatic sources, part of a broader push to boost deportations and curb irregular migration.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands said in September they were working towards a deal with a non-EU country to host "return hubs".

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.
